pr_title: Fall back to using old command when GetServer isn't supported
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/41320

Commit https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/85a090053585a76203eb6ffcdcd6d95d55fba847 added logic to check the server version and decide whether or not to use a deprecated API. It turns out that the `GetServer` call that's being used when determining the version doesn't work in some cases (such as when using Redis behind a proxy).

This change makes it so that we treat a `NotSupportedException` from `GetServer` the same as we'd treat an old version (i.e. by falling back to the deprecated command).

issue_context.title: Caching StackExchangeRedis throws exception when using Twemproxy
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Starting from version 6.0.2 of Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis there is a breaking bug which causes the exception mentioned below to occur when using Redis behind a proxy like Twemproxy.

The bug is caused by commit https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/85a090053585a76203eb6ffcdcd6d95d55fba847. 

Specifically the `_connection.GetServer(endPoint)` call in `ValidateServerFeatures()`. This is call is unsupported when using the build in proxy functionality of StackExchangeRedis, as they have a limited feature set.

The exception is being thrown here: https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/blob/f0fa79c59700a58a1cb848175c544e82ff0d2180/src/StackExchange.Redis/ConnectionMultiplexer.cs#L1021




### Expected Behavior

I expect `IDistributedCache` to keep working when using Redis behind Twemproxy like it did in version 6.0.0 

### Steps To Reproduce

Make use of `IDistributedCache` using Redis behind Twemproxy. No easy way to make a repro project of this.

### Exceptions (if any)

```
System.NotSupportedException: The server API is not available via twemproxy
   at StackExchange.Redis.ConnectionMultiplexer.GetServer(EndPoint endpoint, object asyncState) in /_/src/StackExchange.Redis/ConnectionMultiplexer.cs:line 1504
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis.RedisCache.ValidateServerFeatures()
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis.RedisCache+<ConnectAsync>d__22.MoveNext()
   at System.Runtime.ExceptionServices.ExceptionDispatchInfo.Throw()
   at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.ThrowForNonSuccess(Task task)
   at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.HandleNonSuccessAndDebuggerNotification(Task task)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis.RedisCache+<SetAsync>d__18.MoveNext()
   at System.Runtime.ExceptionServices.ExceptionDispatchInfo.Throw()
   at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.ThrowForNonSuccess(Task task)
   at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.HandleNonSuccessAndDebuggerNotification(Task task)
   at FooBar.FooCache+<SetDistributed>d__22<TItem>.MoveNext() in FooBar/FooCache.cs:line 319
```

### .NET Version

6.0.100

### Anything else?

N/A
comments:
That change https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38715 fixed a regression from 5.0 where Caching.StackExchangeRedis no longer worked with older versions of Redis. If Twemproxy dose not support this call then it did not work prior to .NET 6, and also wouldn't work with older versions of Redis.

For Triage: We can't have it both ways unless we introduce a new option.

We were using Twemproxy with StackExchangeRedis and IDistributedCache just fine in .NET Core 3.1 

Can't you detect if a proxy is being used in StackExchangeRedis and skip that check? This change blocks us from upgrading the package as its breaking. The Redis version behind Twemproxy is irrelevant.
The StackExchange `ConfigurationOptions` provide for defining if it's a proxy for this purpose.  It allows for a reduced featureset.

Triage: we should check if the first invocation of `GetServer` throws and then just use the old set script. It would be nice to log when this happens if that's possible.

Another fix would be to detect if there's a proxy and avoid calling it in the first place.

review_comments: I would also log the error to let users know, as a Warning I'd suggest.
Seems like it's surprisingly non-trivial to get logging added to this project. I'll file an issue for that for now.
